content: The Spoon Theory was conceptualized by Christine Miserandino, a New York-based individual living with lupus and the founder of the website But You Don’t Look Sick. Miserandino sought to find a way to effectively explain to her best friend the daily challenges she faces in managing life with a chronic illness. This theory employs spoons as a metaphorical unit of measurement to represent personal energy. The premise is that individuals with chronic illnesses have a limited number of spoons available each day, and once these spoons are used up, they are left too fatigued to carry out further essential tasks. The article introducing the Spoon Theory remains the most widely-read piece on her website to date. Following the creation of the Spoon Theory, Miserandino established her website and continued her work as a writer and advocate for patients with chronic illnesses. In 2008, Christine Miserandino and her family were recognized by the Lupus Alliance of America for their ongoing efforts to support individuals living with chronic illnesses.
